content.value_statement: Complex projects often contain independent tasks that waste time when handled sequentially. This skill shows how to plan, launch, collect, and synthesize parallel subagent work.
actual_capabilities: Explains when independent tasks can safely run at the same time.
Shows how to launch multiple Task calls in one assistant message.
Describes result retrieval with TaskOutput and synthesis steps.
Provides patterns for task, directory, and perspective based parallelization.
Lists cases where sequential work is safer than parallel work.
limitations: Does not run subagents or manage task state by itself.
Requires a tool environment that supports background Task calls.
Cannot prevent merge conflicts when tasks edit shared files.
Assumes the orchestrator reviews and reconciles all outputs.

use_cases.title: Parallel Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Split independent implementation, testing, and documentation tasks across specialized subagents, then combine the results.

use_cases.title: Multi Angle Code Review
use_cases.description: Run security, performance, testing, and architecture reviews at the same time for faster feedback.

use_cases.title: Repository Exploration
use_cases.description: Assign different directories or modules to separate subagents and synthesize their findings into one overview.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Parallel Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this request and list which tasks can run in parallel. Mark any task that must wait for another result.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Subagent Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Create clear assignments for independent work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one focused subagent prompt for each independent task. Include role, context, files, expected output, and focus areas.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use several review perspectives at the same time.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel review plan with security, performance, testing, and architecture subagents. Explain how their results should be merged.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Conflicting Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these subagent results, resolve conflicts, remove duplicates, and produce one prioritized implementation plan with risks and next actions.

output_examples.input: Plan parallel work for authentication, tests, and documentation.
output_examples.output: A task split that assigns implementation, testing, and documentation to separate subagents, followed by a synthesis step.

output_examples.input: Review a project from security, performance, testing, and architecture perspectives.
output: A retrieval plan for each result.
A final synthesis checklist for conflicts and priorities.

output_examples.input: Decide whether a migration should use parallel execution.
output_examples.output: A decision that separates safe independent checks from sequential migration steps that depend on order.

best_practices: Confirm tasks are independent before launching background subagents.
Give each subagent narrow scope, relevant files, and a clear output format.
Always synthesize results and resolve conflicts before presenting final work.
anti_patterns: Do not parallelize tasks that edit the same files without coordination.
Do not launch dependent tasks before prerequisite results are available.
Do not forward raw subagent outputs without review and deduplication.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you plan and coordinate independent AI subagent tasks that can run at the same time.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guide for orchestrating supported Task tool workflows.

faq.question: When should I avoid parallel execution?
faq.answer: Avoid it when tasks depend on each other, require ordered steps, or modify the same files.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code style agent workflows.

faq.question: How are subagent results handled?
faq.answer: The skill recommends collecting each result, merging related findings, resolving conflicts, and producing one final summary.

faq.question: Does it replace project planning?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning, but the orchestrator must still choose safe task boundaries.
